whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Claim

items.title: You Have Time, But Not Forever
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim. If a government entity is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it helps to get moving early.

items.title: Being Partly at Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the incident. Your recovery is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, in ordinary injury cases. This means compensation isn't automatically limited to medical bills and lost wages.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no fee unless we recover money for you. That removes the financial barrier to getting a professional opinion on your case.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Ross?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a claim. If your injury involved a government vehicle or property, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still pursue compensation even if you share some blame. Your final recovery would just be reduced by your percentage of fault, not blocked entirely.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Ross?
items.answer: Public crash records show reported collision activity concentrated along corridors like Sir Francis Drake Boulevard, Loma Linda Avenue, Ross Common, and Ross Commons, with reports often clustering on Fridays between 10 a.m. and noon. These are simply public-record counts, not a judgment about any particular road.
